Digital Readiness of Small Firms in West Africa: 2024 Report

Kofi Boateng and Aminata Diallo · Published 2 November 2024

Executive summary

This report measures how ready small firms in Ghana, Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire are to use digital and data-driven tools. We combine a survey of 612 firms with 24 interviews with owner-managers and business-association staff. Overall readiness is moderate: most firms use mobile money and messaging apps, but few keep structured digital records, which limits their ability to benefit from analytics or artificial intelligence.

Methodology

The survey sample was drawn from business-association membership lists in six cities, stratified by sector and firm size. Fieldwork ran from February to May 2024. Interviews were semi-structured, lasted about 45 minutes, and were analysed thematically by two researchers working independently. Readiness was scored from 0 to 100 using twelve indicators grouped into infrastructure, skills, records and strategy.

Firms in retail and services scored higher than firms in manufacturing and agriculture. The gap between firms with and without a staff member holding a tertiary qualification was larger than the gap between countries. Only 14% of firms kept digital sales records that could be exported to a spreadsheet.

Interviewees described a "pilot trap": many firms had tried a digital tool through a donor programme, but stopped using it when the free period ended. Association staff said that firms rarely had anyone responsible for technology decisions.

Recommendations

We recommend that business associations offer shared digital record-keeping services, that donor programmes budget for at least two years of support after a pilot, and that national statistics offices add questions on digital records to their enterprise surveys so that progress can be tracked over time.
